messages.subject: adjusting line length and total area surveyed when effort is nul
parts:
Good Day,
=C2=A0
When surveying seals on ice, we sometimes flew over patches of fog (no visi=
bility) or we encountered technical problems with the recorders and lost da=
ta on parts of some lines.
While attending the workshop in Petaluma last September, I mentioned this p=
roblem to one of the instructor and I thought I understood the answer...but=
it seems I was wrong. Here is what I have in my notes, that now seems conf=
using to me:
=C2=A0
1) for fog: no visibility so no effort; the line length should be decreased=
by the parts with fog but total area surveyed should remain the same
2) for technical problems: remove effort by=C2=A0decreasing line length=C2=
=A0AND corresponding area from the total area surveyed as followed: (strip =
width*lenght of line were no data was recorded)+area corresponding to half =
way to the next line
=C2=A0
Why shouldn't I adjust the total area for fog? Why should I remove more are=
a (i.e. half-way to the next line) than the strip surveyed=C2=A0in case of =
technical problems?
=C2=A0
Thank you in advance for your help,
=C2=A0
Magaly
